title: pkg/api control-flow map: construction → route registration → request dispatch
answers: How does a request get from the HTTP mux to a pkg/api handler?
Where are all API routes registered?
What builds the HTTPServer and when do routes get mounted?
What's the difference between response.Response handlers and raw web.Handler handlers?
body:
pkg/api is Grafana's core HTTP API layer: request parsing, auth/RBAC gating, response shaping live here; business logic lives in pkg/services/<domain>.
- Construction: `api.ProvideHTTPServer` (pkg/api/http_server.go) is a Wire provider taking every service dependency; it calls `hs.registerRoutes()` then `hs.declareFixedRoles()`.
- Route declaration: `(hs *HTTPServer) registerRoutes()` (pkg/api/api.go) is the single place all routes are declared via `hs.RouteRegister` (`routing.RouteRegister`, impl in pkg/api/routing/route_register.go), grouped by prefix with shared middleware per group.
- Server start: `(hs *HTTPServer) Run(ctx)` (pkg/api/http_server.go) calls `hs.applyRoutes()`, which first runs `addMiddlewaresAndStaticRoutes()` (installs `hs.ContextHandler.Middleware` building `*contextmodel.ReqContext`, CSRF, recovery, tracing) then `hs.RouteRegister.Register(hs.web, ...)` to mount routes on the `web.Mux`; the route register panics at startup on an exact duplicate method+pattern (pkg/api/routing/route_register.go), so a misplaced route is a build/startup-time failure, not silent.
- Per-request handler signature convention: `func(c *contextmodel.ReqContext) response.Response`, adapted to `web.Handler` via `routing.Wrap` (pkg/api/routing/routing.go), which calls `res.WriteTo(c)` (pkg/api/response/response.go) to write the HTTP response. A minority of legacy/streaming handlers (hs.Index, pkg/api/swagger.go) use the raw `func(c *contextmodel.ReqContext)` signature and write to `c.Resp` directly — don't mix the two without using `routing.Wrap`.
- Newer resources route through pkg/registry/apis/... (k8s-apiserver-backed); domain files with a `_k8s.go` sibling (e.g. pkg/api/datasources_k8s.go) conditionally redirect a legacy handler to the apiserver path based on feature flags — both paths may need updating together.
